sessions.session_title: 💡 Session 1: Welcome to Godot & Engine Setup

points.title: What is Godot?
points.desc: An open-source, highly lightweight, and powerful game engine that uses scenes and nodes to build 2D and 3D games.
points.example: Creating a Node2D root to represent the game world.

points.title: Nodes & Scenes Architecture
points.desc: Everything in Godot is a Node, and groups of nodes are structured hierarchically inside reusable Scenes.

sessions.session_title: 💡 Session 2: Nodes, Scenes, and GDScript Functions

points.title: GDScript Core functions
points.desc: GDScript is Python-like. The _ready() function runs once on startup, and _process(delta) runs once per frame for updates.

points.title: AnimatedSprite2D
points.desc: A specific node to bundle pixel art frames together, allowing you to animate actions like running, jumping, and idling.

points.title: Player Vector Movement
points.desc: Capturing directional keyboard mappings to manipulate coordinate coordinates using built-in Input structures.

sessions.session_title: 💡 Session 5: Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) for Games

points.title: Game Design Document (GDD)
points.desc: A roadmap document detailing how mechanics, sound, levels, and rules interact, ensuring team coordination prior to full coding.
points.example: GDD definition for Pong: defining speed, paddle controls, and boundary collision guidelines.

targets: Set up margins and layout anchors

points.title: Control Nodes & CanvasLayers
points.desc: UI layout nodes like Labels and Buttons remain locked to the viewer screen via CanvasLayers, ignoring camera rotations.

sessions.session_title: 💡 Session 7: User Interface Programming in Godot

points.title: Node Signal Connections
points.desc: Signals are Godot's event system that emit messages when nodes perform actions (like clicking buttons), triggering target functions.

points.title: Audio Streams
points.desc: Triggering sound effect files dynamically to signal events like hits, background tracks, or level transitions to the user.

points.title: Parallax Visual Depth
points.desc: Simulating depth by moving distant layers (like clouds or far buildings) slower than foreground player cameras.
points.example: Set ParallaxLayer scale factors to (0.1, 0.1) for clouds, and (0.8, 0.8) for nearby trees.

sessions.session_title: 💡 Session 10: Building Pong: Part 1 - Mechanics & Physics

points.title: Ball Velocity Calculations
points.desc: Using velocity vector properties and bounce mechanisms inside physical boundaries to keep the ball in motion.

sessions.session_title: 💡 Session 11: Polishing Your Game: VFX & Particles

points.title: Visual FX (VFX) Burst
points.desc: Using GPUParticles2D emitters to spray lightweight coordinate sparkles or dust shapes upon action impacts.

sessions.session_title: 💡 Session 12: Building Pong: Part 2 - Complete Loop

points.title: Win & Goal Check Zones
points.desc: Using Area2D zones to monitor and flag whenever ball body coordinates cross standard goal borders.
